_readme: Edit this file to change the schedule. Each week has a number, a Wednesday date, and either tasks per team, an 'off' reason for no meeting, or 'all' for Showcase or Buffer weeks.

Mechanical.title: Kickoff and Account Setup
items: Pick roles and decide the robot's look and personality as a team
Set up the accounts and software this subteam uses: Onshape
Mechanical.deliv: Robot mood board and every member's Onshape account

Electrical.title: Kickoff and Account Setup
items: Pick roles and decide the robot's look and personality as a team
Set up the accounts and software this subteam uses: TinkerCad, KiCad, and the Arduino IDE with ESP32 board support
Electrical.deliv: Robot mood board, a TinkerCad account for every member, and KiCad and Arduino IDE installed on every laptop

Software.title: Kickoff and Account Setup
items: Pick roles and decide the robot's look and personality as a team
Set up the accounts and software this subteam uses: GitHub, VS Code, and the Arduino IDE with ESP32 board support
Software.deliv: Robot mood board, a GitHub account for every member, and VS Code and Arduino IDE installed on every laptop

Biomedical.title: Kickoff and Account Setup
items: Pick roles and decide the robot's look and personality as a team
Set up the accounts and software this subteam uses: Onshape, GitHub, and the Arduino IDE with ESP32 board support
Biomedical.deliv: Robot mood board, Onshape and GitHub accounts for every member, and Arduino IDE installed on every laptop

Mechanical.title: Concept Design and Cardboard Prototypes
items: Whole subteam sketches the body and arm at 6 to 7 inches tall
Body Pair builds a cardboard body to check size, proportions, and component space
Arm Pair builds a cardboard arm and claw with string to test routing, claw motion, and elbow bend
Mechanical.deliv: Concept sketch, cardboard body, and working cardboard arm

Electrical.title: Electrical Concept Design and Parts Selection
items: Map the full signal chain as a block diagram, from electrodes to the ESP32 and from the battery to every part
Learn to read a datasheet using the real parts
Finalize the parts order list
Circuit basics are covered at the breadboarding workshop this week
Electrical.deliv: Block diagram and parts order list

Software.title: Software Concept Design
items: Map how the robot "thinks" as a flowchart: idle, correct muscle, wrong muscle, and both at once
Work with the team to list every face expression the robot needs
Software.deliv: Software flowchart and face expression list

Biomedical.title: Cuff Concept Design
items: Sketch cuff designs and build a quick cardboard and fabric mockup
Decide which cuff parts will be 3D printed, like electrode holders and the board housing

Mechanical.title: Onshape Training Part 1
items: Guided training on sketches, constraints, and extrudes

Electrical.title: Op Amps
items: Quick TinkerCad demo, then build a non inverting amplifier with the TL272 and check the gain with a multimeter
Build an op amp comparator that turns on an LED past a set voltage
Electrical.deliv: Working amplifier and comparator LED circuit

Software.title: Arduino C++ Basics
items: Learn variables, if statements, loops, and functions by building
Read a potentiometer, graph it on the Serial Plotter, and use it to control an LED's brightness

Biomedical.title: Onshape Training
items: Join Mechanical for guided training on sketches, constraints, and extrudes

Mechanical.title: Onshape Training Part 2
items: Guided training on assemblies and mates
Measure real components (servos, ESP32, OLED, battery) and model them as simple blocks

Electrical.title: Filters
items: Build RC low pass and high pass filters on a breadboard
Use an ESP32 and the Arduino Serial Plotter as a simple oscilloscope to see a signal before and after filtering
Electrical.deliv: Working filters with plotted before and after signals

Software.title: Servos and the OLED
items: Controls Pair makes a servo sweep, then controls a servo with a potentiometer
Wireless Pair gets the OLED displaying text and simple shapes
Software.deliv: Potentiometer controlled servo and working OLED

Biomedical.title: Forearm Anatomy and Muscle Mapping
items: Learn the forearm flexors and extensors, then find them on each other by feel
Mark candidate electrode sites

Mechanical.title: v1 CAD and First Prints
items: Arm Pair CADs the arm, elbow joint, servo mounts, and claw, and finalizes string tension and pull distance
Body Pair CADs the body with space for the battery, ESP32, servos, OLED window, and LED holes, plus servo brackets and board standoffs
Leads send both to the Makerspace after the meeting
Mechanical.deliv: Arm, claw, and body v1 CAD models in the print queue

Electrical.title: First Build
items: Cuff Pair builds the instrumentation amplifier and bandpass filter for channel 1 and views the output on the Serial Plotter
Robot Pair works through the schematic section of a KiCad course, then designs the robot power system (battery, charging module, voltage regulator)
Electrical.deliv: Channel 1 front end and robot power schematic

Software.title: Faces and Wireless Basics
items: Controls Pair draws the happy, confused, and idle faces on the OLED
Wireless Pair sends a simple message between two ESP32s over Bluetooth
Software.deliv: Three face expressions and a working ESP32 to ESP32 link

Biomedical.title: Electrodes and Calibration Concepts
items: Biosignal Pair learns electrode types, spacing, reference placement, and skin prep, then practices placement
Calibration Pair learns resting signals, maximum flex, and thresholds, then drafts the calibration steps
Biomedical.deliv: Draft electrode placement and calibration protocols

Mechanical.title: Prototype Testing
items: Arm Pair tests elbow range of motion and claw open and close with a servo sweep
Body Pair checks body fit with the component reference models
Write the spring fix list
Mechanical.deliv: Tested prototypes and a spring fix list

Electrical.title: Signal Chain and Power Build
items: Cuff Pair adds the rectifier, envelope detector, and comparator, then tests on a forearm with Biomedical
Robot Pair builds and tests the power system on a breadboard
Electrical.deliv: Working channel 1 signal and verified robot voltages

Software.title: Fake Muscles and End to End Demo
items: Wireless Pair sends two potentiometer values wirelessly as the two muscle signals
Controls Pair codes the response logic: correct muscle means happy face and movement, wrong or both means confused face and no movement
Connect both halves so turning a potentiometer on one ESP32 makes the robot ESP32 react
Software.deliv: Full system demo with fake signals

Biomedical.title: First Real EMG
items: Calibration Pair writes simple Arduino code to log signal readings
Test candidate electrode sites on a forearm with Electrical's channel 1 circuit and log which sites give the strongest, cleanest signal
Biomedical.deliv: Logging code, site comparison data, and chosen sites

Mechanical.title: Spring Kickoff
items: Get final board size limits from Electrical

Electrical.title: Channel 2 and LEDs
items: Cuff Pair builds channel 2 and debugs both channels with Biomedical
Robot Pair builds the LED signal strength circuit
Agree on maximum board sizes with Mechanical and Biomedical
Electrical.deliv: Two working EMG channels, working LED circuit, and board size limits

Software.title: Spring Kickoff and Calibration Plan
items: Clean up and comment fall code and set up a shared GitHub repository
Measure the delay between input and response
Plan the calibration approach with Biomedical
Software.deliv: Shared code repository, delay measurement, and calibration plan

Biomedical.title: Two Channel Test and Cuff CAD
items: Calibration Pair tests both channels with Electrical and checks that flexing one muscle doesn't trigger the other, then finalizes electrode sites
Biosignal Pair CADs the cuff, including electrode holders, strap mounts, and a housing for Electrical's board and battery
Biomedical.deliv: Confirmed independent channels, final sites, and cuff CAD

Mechanical.title: Body v2
items: Redesign the body around real Electrical components
Mechanical.deliv: Body v2 CAD with a fit check from Electrical

Electrical.title: Schematics and PCB Layout
items: Cuff Pair works through the schematic section of the KiCad course, then draws the cuff schematic
Robot Pair adds the LED circuit to the robot schematic
Both pairs start the PCB layout section of the course
Electrical.deliv: Final KiCad schematics and started board layouts

Software.title: Calibration Mode
items: Code a calibration routine with Biomedical that records resting and max flex signals and sets thresholds
Software.deliv: Working calibration mode with fake signals

Biomedical.title: Calibration Mode
items: Calibration Pair codes the calibration routine with Software
Biosignal Pair sends the cuff parts to print
Biomedical.deliv: Working calibration mode with fake signals and cuff parts in the print queue

Mechanical.title: Reprints
items: Print body v2 and arm v2 with fall fixes

Electrical.title: Finish Layout, Review, and Order
items: Finish both layouts using through hole parts, 2 layers, and a compact size
Run KiCad's design rules check and review both boards as a full team
Order bare boards

Software.title: Smoothing and Polish
items: Add signal smoothing to reduce jitter
Polish the face animations
Software.deliv: Smoother response and finished face set

Biomedical.title: Cuff Assembly
items: Assemble the printed parts with straps and electrode snaps

Mechanical.title: Arm Integration
items: Mount servos and test the arm with Software's control code

Electrical.title: Signal to ESP32
items: Connect the breadboard EMG output to the cuff ESP32 with Software and match voltage levels
Electrical.deliv: Clean signal readings in Software's code

Software.title: Signal to ESP32
items: Read the real EMG output from Electrical's circuit and match voltage levels together
Share servo control code with Mechanical for arm integration

Biomedical.title: Test Protocol
items: Write the full user test protocol, including calibration steps, tasks, and what to measure
Choose club member volunteers as testers
Biomedical.deliv: Final test protocol and tester list

Mechanical.title: Claw Tuning
items: Tune string tension so the claw works reliably with live EMG control

Electrical.title: Soldering Day
items: Soldering training, then solder components onto the PCBs
Backup plan: solder onto perfboard if the boards haven't arrived

Software.title: Real EMG Control
items: Replace fake signals with real ones and drive the claw with live EMG alongside Mechanical
Software.deliv: Claw controlled by real muscle signals

Biomedical.title: Calibration with Real Signals
items: Run calibration with real EMG signals and adjust the code and steps as needed

Mechanical.title: Face and LED Mounting
items: Fit the OLED face and LEDs into the body with Software and Electrical
Mechanical.deliv: Face and LEDs securely mounted and visible

Electrical.title: Board Testing and Cuff Power
items: Test each soldered board and fix any issues
Add the battery and regulator to the cuff and fit the board with Biomedical's cuff design
Electrical.deliv: Working PCBs and a wireless, battery powered cuff

Software.title: Face and LED Mounting
items: Test the OLED and LEDs once mounted in the body with Mechanical and Electrical
Software.deliv: Face clearly visible and working inside the robot

Biomedical.title: Cuff Fit and Comfort
items: Fit Electrical's board and battery into the cuff and test comfort on several testers

Mechanical.title: Full Assembly v1
items: Install all electronics inside the body

Electrical.title: Full Assembly v1
items: Install the robot board, LEDs, and OLED wiring inside the body with Mechanical and Software

Software.title: Full Assembly v1
items: Load final code onto both ESP32s in the assembled robot and cuff

Biomedical.title: Full Assembly v1
items: Do a first full run of the protocol on the assembled robot

Mechanical.title: System Testing
items: Test with Biomedical's users and log mechanical failures

Electrical.title: System Testing
items: Test signal quality across Biomedical's users and log noise issues

Software.title: System Testing
items: Test with Biomedical's users and log delays, misreads, and dropped connections

Biomedical.title: System Testing
items: Run the test protocol with club member testers, recording success rate and how quickly each person learns control

Mechanical.title: Iteration
items: Reprint and fix fit and durability issues

Electrical.title: Iteration
items: Fix noise problems and adjust gain with Biomedical's calibration results

Software.title: Iteration
items: Tune thresholds and response logic and reduce delay

Biomedical.title: Data Analysis
items: Analyze results and share calibration findings with Electrical and Software

Mechanical.title: Kid Friendly Finish
items: Add personality details, smooth edges, and finish the look

Electrical.title: Reliability Testing
items: Test battery life and check connections under repeated use

Software.title: Kid Friendly Features
items: Add reward animations, like a celebration when a child gets several in a row

Biomedical.title: Round 2 Testing
items: Retest after the fixes and compare to Round 1
Reprint any cuff parts that need changes

Mechanical.title: Durability and Spares
items: Stress test moving parts and print spare claw and arm pieces

Electrical.title: Documentation and Spares
items: Create a wiring diagram and solder a spare set of boards from the extras in your order

Software.title: Edge Cases and Documentation
items: Handle a lost Bluetooth connection with a "sleepy" face and automatic reconnect
Finish code comments and a README

Biomedical.title: Clinical Context and User Guide
items: Write a short guide on how a therapist and child would use the robot, including calibration

Mechanical.title: Showcase Prep
items: Build a display stand and rehearse the demo
Finalize documentation and resume bullets

Electrical.title: Showcase Prep
items: Build a display with a bare PCB, its schematic, and waveform screenshots from each stage
Rehearse the demo and finalize resume bullets
Electrical.deliv: Signal chain display and demo ready electronics

Software.title: Showcase Prep
items: Build a demo mode and a live signal display on a laptop for visitors
Rehearse the demo and finalize resume bullets

Biomedical.title: Showcase Prep
items: Build a poster with the problem, electrode sites, and test results
Rehearse the demo and finalize resume bullets
Biomedical.deliv: Results poster and demo ready cuff
